title: Semantic Condition Checking
summary: Evaluate meaning-dependent workflow conditions through evidence-backed classification while keeping hard business predicates deterministic and reviewable.
overview: Semantic condition checking decides whether unstructured evidence satisfies a workflow condition, such as whether a customer has supplied a complete explanation or whether a document describes an exception. It is useful when exact string matching cannot capture meaning. The result should be a structured decision with evidence spans, an uncertainty state, and a versioned rubric.

Keep semantic classification separate from deterministic facts. Whether an amount exceeds a limit or a user has approval authority should be checked in code or policy. A semantic judge can establish that text appears to express consent, but it cannot independently establish that the speaker is authenticated or legally authorized.

production.poc: A prototype can label representative examples and compare rules, embeddings, and model-based classification. Include ambiguous and contradictory examples rather than only obvious matches.
production.production: Production requires an abstention path, evidence references, stable rubrics, and thresholds calibrated to the cost of false acceptance versus false rejection.
production.scale: At scale, evaluate performance by language, document type, and business segment. Monitor distribution changes and reviewer reversals because a classifier can remain confident while the meaning of operational language shifts.

components.name: Condition registry
components.role: Defines the semantic question, accepted labels, required evidence, and uncertainty behavior.

components.name: Evidence selector
components.role: Supplies relevant authorized text with provenance and preserves enough surrounding context.

components.name: Semantic evaluator
components.role: Produces a structured label and supporting spans under the versioned rubric.

components.name: Deterministic gate
components.role: Combines semantic output with verified facts, permissions, and hard business rules.

components.name: Review queue
components.role: Resolves ambiguous or high-impact decisions and records adjudicated outcomes.

flow.title: Define condition
flow.description: Express the intended meaning and enumerate positive, negative, ambiguous, and contradictory examples.

flow.title: Select evidence
flow.description: Retrieve relevant text with source identifiers and sufficient context to avoid misleading fragments.

flow.title: Classify semantics
flow.description: Request a constrained label with evidence spans and an explicit unknown option.

flow.title: Verify support
flow.description: Check that cited spans exist and that the classifier did not substitute unrelated evidence.

flow.title: Apply hard rules
flow.description: Combine the semantic result with deterministic identity, amount, date, and policy checks.

flow.title: Route uncertainty
flow.description: Continue, reject, or request review according to calibrated decision costs and task risk.

diagrams.title: Semantic judgment inside a deterministic gate

diagrams.caption: Meaning classification supplies one input to the gate; trusted business predicates remain separate.

useCase.title: Checking whether a claim explanation addresses missing facts
useCase.situation: A claims team asks customers to explain the circumstances of an incident before assigning a specialist reviewer.
useCase.problem: Simple keyword checks accept irrelevant narratives and reject valid explanations phrased in unfamiliar language.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must determine whether the response addresses required factual questions without deciding coverage or credibility.
useCase.architecture: A semantic evaluator checks each required question, cites supporting spans, and passes labels to a deterministic completeness gate.
runtime: A customer response is segmented by incident time, location, and sequence; each condition receives supported, missing, or ambiguous status.
Only verified completeness advances the administrative workflow; unresolved meaning generates a targeted follow-up question.
useCase.failure: If the text contains contradictory dates, the evaluator returns ambiguity and preserves both spans rather than selecting one silently.
useCase.impact: Measure false-complete decisions, unnecessary follow-ups, reviewer disagreement, and performance by language. Completeness is not proof that the customer's account is true.

tradeoffs.benefit: Natural language variation can be handled without large keyword lists.
tradeoffs.cost: Decisions remain probabilistic and need calibration.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reviewers can inspect why a condition was considered met.
tradeoffs.cost: Relevant context may extend beyond a short quoted span.

tradeoffs.benefit: Ambiguous cases avoid unsafe automatic advancement.
tradeoffs.cost: Review volume increases when thresholds are conservative.

failures.scenario: A positive label cites nonexistent text
failures.detection: Span validation cannot locate the claimed evidence.
failures.recovery: Reject the classification and retry once or route to review.

failures.scenario: One language has high false rejection
failures.detection: Segmented evaluation reveals a distribution-specific gap.
failures.recovery: Adjust the model or rubric and use review until validated.

mistakes.mistake: Using a semantic model for numeric thresholds
mistakes.fix: Evaluate exact values in deterministic code.

mistakes.mistake: Forcing every case into yes or no
Treating evidence presence as factual truth
mistakes.fix: Keep completeness, credibility, and authorization separate.

whenToUse: Workflow conditions depend on meaning in unstructured text.
Representative labeled examples can calibrate decisions.
Ambiguous cases have a practical review path.
whenNotToUse: An exact business predicate already determines the answer.
False acceptance is intolerable and no review exists.
The evidence cannot be attributed to a trustworthy source.
checklist: Include ambiguous and contradictory test cases.
Calibrate by decision cost and segment.
